To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

higher levels of total physical activity are associated (in a cross-sectional analysis) with lower insulin areas under oral glucose tolerance curves in a population of Hispanic and non-Hispnic white men and women (n = 219) with impaired glucose tolerance.
higher levels of total physical activity are associated (independently) with lower insulin areas among individuals with impaired glucose intolerance in a community setting.
in a population with impaired glucose tolerance, physical activity is related to insulin resistance as measured by insulin area under the curve.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between habitual physical activity, obesity, and insulin resistance among Hispanic and non-Hispnic white individuals with impaired glucose intolerance.
the relationship between physical activity and glucose tolerance in a rural population.
the effects of physical activity on insulin action in individuals who are at risk for developing non-insulin-dependent (type 2) diabetes mellitus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
physical activity is associated with a lower risk of diabetes, and that this relationship is mediated by a lower risk of insulin resistance.
higher levels of regular physical activity are associated in a population of subjects with IGT with lower values of the insulin area under the curve.
physical activity is a major factor in the development of diabetes and that it should be encouraged in the general population and especially in those at risk for diabetes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
physical activity has an important impact on insulin action in individuals at high risk of non-insulindependent diabetes mellitus.

physical activity is an important factor in the prevention of type 2 diabetes mellitus and that the benefits of physical activity are not restricted to the prevention of obesity but may also include improved glucose metabolism and insulin action.

higher levels of total physical activity are associated independently with lower insulin areas among individuals with IGT, even after controlling for obesity, fat distribution (i.e., waist-to-hip ratio), and age.
The main takeaway from our work is that
individuals with IGT can reduce their risk of diabetes and heart disease by engaging in physical activity, even if they are overweight or obese.
higher levels of regular physical activity are associated lower levels of insulin resistance among individuals with impaired glucose metabolism.
physical activity can be an effective intervention to prevent or delay diabetes and the cardiovascular disease that often accompanies it.
